// Guard fixture: the concatenation hole.
//
// Narrowing the population to "the table after FROM, JOIN, INTO or
// UPDATE" is what keeps a retention policy key out of the registry. It
// also opens a hiding place: split the clause keyword and the table name
// into different literals and the table is named with nothing before it.
//
// The guard reports this rather than dropping it. A guard that silently
// ignores what it cannot parse is exactly the hiding place it was built
// to remove.

package fixture

// SplitQuery assembles the FROM clause across two literals.
func SplitQuery(hostID string) string {
	return `SELECT count(*) FROM ` + `host_rule_state WHERE host_id = $1`
}
